To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the octameric structure (Umezurike, 1975) of beta-glusosidase from B. theobromae is maintained under mildly alkaline (pH 7.5) conditions, but that the pH of the solution of beta-glusocidase A is critical for its stability and that it dissociates into lower-Mr forms at mildly alkaline pH.

the octamer is the basic unit of the enzyme, and that the dissociation products of the octamer are the monomer, the dimer and the tetramer, and that the octamer can be reassembled from the dissociation products.
beta-glucosides A, B, C and D are octamers of Mr 320,000, 160,000, 80,000 and 40,000 respectively and that the octamer dissociates into the smaller forms on incubation in mildly alkaline conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular properties of beta-glucocidase from Botyrodipodia theobromoe Pat.
the molecular properties of the various forms (A-D) of beta-glucoseidase from Botryo-diplodia theobomae.
a study of the molecular forms of beta-glucoseidase from Botrodiplodia theobromoe Pat., and their properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
beta-glucoside hydrolysis by beta-glucosides from Botryodiploida theobromae is a function of an octameric protein.
beta-glucosides A, B, C and D are all octameric forms of beta-glucoseidase.
the octameric structure is the native structure of beta-glucoseidase A, and the dissociation of beta-glucosiidase A into the lower-Mt forms is due to a conformational change induced by a pH shift.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the course of the action of beta-glucanase and beta-glucanases, the beta-1,4-linkages in the glucan chain are broken down, and beta-glucose is released.
the octameric structure is a reversible equilibrium between a tetrameric (Mr 160 000) and a dimeric (Mr 80 000) structure.
beta-glucoside hydrolase is an octameric protein with a molecular mass of 320,000, which dissociates into four subunits of 80,000, two subunits of 40,000 and one subunit of 10,800.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the octameric structure can be maintained in the absence of L-arginine at the active site of beta-glucodisase, provided the pH is maintained below 6.5.
the structure of the enzyme is highly flexible and can be modified to suit the needs of the organism.
we have identified the molecular basis of the resistance of B. theobromae β-glucosides to the inactivating action of the alkaline pH and high temperatures.
